children: Inspire Brands has named the head of its Dunkin' unit as its interim chief executive officer ahead of the company's initial public offering.

Dunkin' President Scott Murphy will temporarily run the Inspire Brands, while CEO Paul Brown takes temporary medical leave, according to a WSJ report  on Wednesday, which cited a message to employees. Brown, Inspire's co-founder, is recovering from a recent injury.
Inspire Brands is considering an IPO as the early as the end of this year, though it could be pushed to early next year, the WSJ reported last month.
Inspire Brands, the owner of Dunkin', Jimmy John's, and Buffalo Wild Wings,
Atlanta-based Inspire Brands has more than 33,000 restaurants worldwide and sales of $33.4 billion.
A publicly traded Inspire Brands, which also owns Arby's and Sonic, would be a trading peer with Starbucks
as well as other multi-restaurant chain operators such as Restaurant Brands International
